ilmara_falls.note: The opening: the elder notices the player, then the Red Fleet takes the crystal chamber. The fight itself is ordinary combat between the soldiers and the (pacifist) acolytes; ilmara_aftermath plays when the last acolyte falls.

beats.text: The elder of Ilmara looks up from the altar and sees you. Every line of her goes still.
[[YELLOW]]The elder of Ilmara speaks, her voice unsteady:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"You... you! Why... why are you here?"[[/]]
The doors of the crystal chamber burst inward, and the Red Fleet pours in behind you, steel drawn, boots loud on pale stone.
A second soldier comes through the doors, and stops to look at the room.
[[RED]]The last of the soldiers fans out across the chamber.[[/]]

leave_ilmara.note: The crystal is taken; the Cinder climbs away, and the soldiers cannot look at one another. It ends on the first fight.

beats.text: The crystal is cold in your hands, and heavier than it has any right to be.
[[YELLOW]]The elder of Ilmara speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Take it, then. You carry our grief out of the door with it. Tell your king that the Water does not forgive."[[/]]
You do not answer. The soldiers fall in around you, and nobody speaks until the wind of the deck is on your face.
The Cinder climbs. Ilmara shrinks behind you to a smear of white stone, and then to nothing.
[[YELLOW]]Red Fleet soldier speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Captain... they did not even lift a hand."[[/]]
[[YELLOW]]Red Fleet soldier speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"We were told they were a threat. Those were priests."[[/]]
You look at the blue light of the crystal on their faces. [[BLUE]]"It had to be done,"[[/]] you say, and nobody believes it, least of all you.
[[YELLOW]]Red Fleet soldier shouts:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Captain! Something in the cloud, off the bow! Monsters!"[[/]]
[[RED]]A horn sounds from the bow. Something dark is coming out of the cloud.[[/]]
A second shape rises beside it.

second_wave.note: A short while after the first fight is won, the sky is not finished with the Cinder.

beats.text: The last wyvern tumbles away into the cloud. The deck is quiet but for the wind and the soldiers' breathing.
[[YELLOW]]Red Fleet soldier speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Is that all of them?"[[/]]
[[RED]]The wind turns. The cloud ahead darkens, and something much larger than a wyvern swings toward the Cinder.[[/]]
Its mate is close behind.
A wyvern circles low under the hull, waiting for you to look the other way.

landing.note: The sky is quiet again. Home, and the chancellor who walks you to the king.

beats.text: The hawks fall, and the cloud closes over them. For a long moment nobody says a word.
Ahead, through the haze, the red banners of Varenholt: the castle on its crag, the docks, the fleet at its moorings.
The Cinder settles onto its mooring with a long groan of timber. You walk down the gangplank with the crystal under your arm.
[[YELLOW]]The chancellor speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"Captain. How good to see you in one piece. And the crystal: splendid. His Majesty has been waiting."[[/]]
The chancellor leads you north.
The chancellor leads you north.
[[YELLOW]]The chancellor speaks:[[/]] [[GREEN]]"His Majesty is waiting, Captain. Tell him of your journey and of the crystal; he will want to hear all of it. Speak to the king."[[/]] (talk king)

night_in_the_castle.note: After the king and Kessa: a night in your own quarters, and dawn with Kessa at the gate.

beats.text: Your quarters are exactly as you left them, and they feel like somebody else's.
You lie down in your armour. The crystal's blue light is still behind your eyes, and under it, the song that stopped.
Somewhere in the castle a door closes. The airships creak at their moorings. Sleep comes anyway, as it always does.
[[CYAN]]The night passes.[[/]]
Grey light at the window. From somewhere below comes a familiar voice, shouting at a quartermaster: Kessa is already at the gate.

ilmara_aftermath.note: Plays when the last acolyte of Ilmara falls.

beats.text: Your own hands are steady. That is the worst of it.
Only the elder of Ilmara is left standing, one hand flat against the altar, looking at you and not at the soldiers.
The Water Crystal burns blue on its altar. The king's order was two words long: bring it. (take crystal)
